Search an airport, or an item, to see how often OPDI has each main item
there, how close it is to the records, and what limits it. The figures are
those of the three days measured; the references are explained on
[Accuracy and availability](index.qmd).

## How to read a card {#how-to-read}

Each item has two labels, kept apart: availability (`high`, `partial`,
`low`) and accuracy (`good`, `fair`, `limited`, `too few compared`,
`no reference`), each with the count it is computed over. The rules are in
[How to read the labels](index.qmd#how-to-read-the-labels). Departure items
are counted among the departures, arrival items among the arrivals.

**Outside Europe there are no airport records: most items show availability
only** (see [Per item](#per-item)). Nothing confirms a take-off time or a stand at an airport in
the United States or in Asia. An item found there may still be wrong. A low
share means the item is mostly missing, for example because the receivers
around the airport do not hear aircraft low down or on the ground; a high
share says only that it exists.

## Which airports {#which-airports}

- **European list:** the 100 European airports with the most departures and
  arrivals in the Network Manager records. Of them, 72 send airport records;
  at the other 28, take-off and landing times are compared with Network
  Manager, and block times, runways and stands have no reference.
- **Worldwide list:** the 100 airports with the most departures and arrivals
  in OPDI's own flight list. Of them, 70 are outside Europe and 30 in Europe,
  28 of which send airport records. The ranking favours the regions where
  OpenSky has many receivers.

An airport in both lists appears once, with both ranks and its European
figures.

## Per item {#per-item}

Type an item's name in the search, or click one of the item chips, to see
every airport grouped by its label. Outside Europe the departure and
destination airports are compared with Network Manager, which knows only the
flights to and from Europe, so only for those flights; the other items have
no reference there.

## Patterns {#patterns}

The patterns and the three lists below cover the European airports only.

**Take-off and landing times** are good at most airports. **Block times and
stands** are the weak items: at most airports they are low in availability,
and where they can be compared, the off-block time is mostly labelled
limited (it is often later than the record), the in-block time more often
fair. **Departure and destination airports** are good almost everywhere.

{{< include _generated/europe_patterns.md >}}

### Where an item is unreliable {#unreliable}

At these airports an item was compared with the records at least 30 times
and fewer than half of OPDI's values agree with them. Do not use the item
there without checking it.

{{< include _generated/europe_limited.md >}}

Two cases stand out:

- At Bergen (`ENBR`), Stavanger (`ENZV`) and Trondheim (`ENVA`), the
  runway OPDI names never agrees with the record, while the take-off and
  landing times there mostly do. This suggests that the runways are named
  differently in OPDI's runway table and in the records, rather than that
  the aircraft used other runways; it has not been checked. Do not use
  `rwy_dep`, `rwy_arr` or `info.runway` at these airports.
- At Malta (`LMML`), most take-off times and most runways disagree with the
  records, while the landing times mostly agree. Do not use the take-off
  times or the runways there.
- At İstanbul Airport (`LTFM`), OPDI has a take-off time for almost no
  departure and a landing time for fewer than half of the arrivals. Positions
  near Istanbul are often disturbed (spoofed), which is possibly the cause.

### Where ground events are nearly absent {#ground-reception}

At these 38 airports, fewer than 2 % of OPDI's departures have an
off-block time and fewer than 2 % of its arrivals an in-block time: the
receivers near the airport hear almost no aircraft on the ground. Block
times, stands and the airport surface events are then missing, not wrong.
Take-off and landing times can still exist, because they need reception
only near the runway in the air.

{{< include _generated/europe_ground.md >}}

### Where no take-off or landing time exists {#no-times}

At these 10 airports OPDI has no take-off time and no landing time on any of the three days, although its flight list has flights there. At
most of them OPDI also gives the airport as destination for only a small
share of the recorded arrivals. The cause has not been established; do not
use these airports for runway or arrival studies.

{{< include _generated/europe_no_times.md >}}
